title: ASU LLM Evaluation Pipeline
description: Automated CI/CD pipeline that scores a university RAG chatbot across 100 test questions on every code push, enforcing 6 quality gates with results streamed to a live React dashboard.
longDescription: An automated LLM quality monitoring system for an ASU university RAG chatbot. Every GitHub push triggers a full RAGAS evaluation: GPT-4o answers 100 test questions, GPT-4o-mini judges each response for faithfulness, relevancy, and context precision — 25× cheaper than GPT-4o for evaluation tasks. Six automated quality gates block deployment if any metric drops below threshold (hallucination rate ≤ 10%, faithfulness ≥ 0.80, answer relevancy ≥ 0.75). Vectors persist in Pinecone cloud so CI runners skip re-embedding on every push. Results are auto-committed back to the repo with [skip ci] to prevent infinite trigger loops, then streamed to a React dashboard on Vercel showing trend charts across the last 50 runs, a per-question breakdown table with category and difficulty filters, and real-time cost tracking with 30-second auto-refresh. Latest run: 6/6 gates PASS, faithfulness 1.00, hallucination 0%, cost $0.087.
highlights: 6 automated quality gates block CI deployment: faithfulness ≥ 0.80, hallucination ≤ 10%, relevancy ≥ 0.75, context precision ≥ 0.60, latency p95 ≤ 15s, cost ≤ $0.02/query
GPT-4o-mini as judge — 25× cheaper than GPT-4o with negligible quality loss; full 100-question run costs ~$0.87 vs ~$21.75
Pinecone cloud vector store eliminates per-run re-embedding; CI checks vector_count > 0 before upload
Auto-commits results JSON with [skip ci] back to repo; React dashboard on Vercel auto-refreshes every 30s
Trend charts across 50 runs + per-question breakdown table with category, difficulty, and PASS/FAIL filters

title: TravelIQ
description: Multi-model travel optimization pipeline combining crowd forecasting, sentiment analysis, and constraint-based routing for personalized itinerary generation.
longDescription: TravelIQ is an end-to-end travel intelligence pipeline that fuses three independent data signals into a single decision layer. A SARIMAX model forecasts crowd density for 20+ tourist locations using historical visit patterns and seasonal trends. DistilBERT processes live traveler reviews to extract sentiment signals that adjust location scores in real time. An Open-Meteo weather layer adds suitability scoring based on current and forecast conditions. Finally, Google OR-Tools solves a Vehicle Routing Problem to generate constraint-satisfying, personalized itineraries, balancing crowd avoidance, weather comfort, and user preferences from raw data to a final ranked plan.
highlights: SARIMAX-based crowd density forecasting for 20+ tourist locations
Transformer-based sentiment analysis using DistilBERT for real-time reviews
Constraint-based VRP optimization using Google OR-Tools
Weather suitability scoring using Open-Meteo API
End-to-end pipeline from data ingestion to itinerary output

title: Republic of Bean
description: Multi-agent AI platform where GPT-4 agents with distinct political personas debate policy, vote, and generate structured outcome reports.
longDescription: Republic of Bean is a multi-agent simulation platform where autonomous GPT-4 agents, each engineered with a distinct ideological persona, who engage in structured parliamentary debates, cast votes, and produce analytical outcome reports. The project explores persona engineering, structured LLM outputs, and multi-agent coordination: how independent AI actors with different priors reach (or fail to reach) consensus. Built as a full-stack Next.js application with TypeScript, it demonstrates real-world patterns in agentic AI design: role prompting, turn-based orchestration, and automated report synthesis from multi-agent deliberation.
highlights: Autonomous AI agents with distinct political personas powered by GPT-4
Real-time parliamentary debate simulation
Automated policy outcome report generation
Structured voting system with faction-based alignment scoring
Full-stack Next.js application with TypeScript

title: Anomaly Detection in Crowds
description: CNN-based crowd safety system that learns normal behavior from video and flags anomalies in real time with frame-level heatmaps.
longDescription: A deep learning pipeline for detecting abnormal crowd behavior in public spaces. The system trains a convolutional neural network on historical crowd footage to learn what normal activity looks like, then scores incoming frames against that learned baseline in real time. Anomalies are surfaced with configurable sensitivity thresholds and visualized as frame-level heatmaps that highlight exactly where unusual activity is occurring, making it actionable for safety operators rather than just a binary alert.
highlights: CNN-based baseline behavior learning from historical crowd footage
Real-time image correlation for anomaly scoring
Configurable sensitivity thresholds for different deployment environments
Frame-level anomaly heatmap visualization
Batch and streaming inference modes

title: AI Voice Turing Test Model
description: Audio ML + NLP classifier that distinguishes human from AI-generated calls, built for the ASU Social Bias Hackathon (3rd place).
longDescription: Built for the Social Bias Hackathon hosted by Ethical Spectacle Research and Arizona State University. The system combines an audio feature pipeline (MFCCs, pitch, cadence, spectral entropy extracted with Librosa) with NLP sentiment analysis on call transcripts to classify whether a caller is human or AI-generated. Beyond classification accuracy, the project included a demographic bias audit: evaluating whether the model's error rates varied across population groups and documenting those disparities. Earned 3rd place recognition from ASU and Ethical Spectacle Research.
highlights: 🏆 3rd Place, ASU Social Bias Hackathon
Audio feature extraction: MFCCs, pitch, cadence, spectral features
NLP sentiment analysis for transcript-based signals
Bias analysis across demographic categories
Interactive demo for real-time call classification

title: Heart Disease Detection
description: Supervised ML classifier achieving 85% accuracy on the Cleveland Heart Disease dataset, with full model benchmarking and SHAP feature analysis.
longDescription: A heart disease prediction pipeline built on the Cleveland Heart Disease dataset. The project covers the full supervised learning workflow: data cleaning, feature scaling, categorical encoding, then benchmarking three classifiers: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbors, using cross-validation. The best model reached 85% accuracy. SHAP values were used to interpret which features drove predictions, making the model's behavior transparent rather than just measuring its performance.
highlights: 85% classification accuracy on Cleveland Heart Disease dataset
Comparative analysis: Logistic Regression vs Random Forest vs KNN
Feature importance analysis and SHAP explanations
Full preprocessing pipeline with cross-validation

title: Shaded Route Planning
description: City-scale shade simulation that scores pedestrian walking routes by sun coverage across different times of day.
longDescription: A heat-aware pedestrian routing system designed for urban environments where sun exposure is a real comfort and safety concern. The system uses solar geometry modeling to compute sun angles throughout the day, then applies image segmentation to estimate building shadow coverage at street level. Walking routes are scored by their shade percentage at a given time of day, enabling route recommendations that prioritize cooler, shadier paths, a practical application of geospatial reasoning and computational geometry.
highlights: City-scale shade simulation using solar geometry models
Time-of-day aware shade prediction for walking paths
Image segmentation for building shadow estimation
Route scoring based on shade coverage percentage

title: Industrial AI Copilot for Equipment Monitoring
description: Production real-time anomaly detection system for industrial equipment with sub-second alerting and a full automated incident response pipeline.
longDescription: A production-grade equipment monitoring platform that tracks four live sensor streams — temperature, pressure, vibration, and flow rate — and detects anomalies with sub-second latency. What makes this more than a detection demo is the full incident lifecycle that follows: an audio alert fires via Web Audio API, an automated work order is generated, and a technician notification email is dispatched via Resend — all without manual intervention. To validate the system before deployment, an anomaly injection simulator was built to stress-test edge cases and failure modes. The entire platform is deployed on Vercel with live SWR data fetching.
highlights: Sub-second anomaly detection alerting across 4 sensor types (temperature, pressure, vibration, flow rate)
Full incident lifecycle: audio alerts → automated work orders → technician email via Resend
Anomaly injection simulator for edge-case testing and failure mode validation
Deployed on Vercel with real-time SWR data fetching and live dashboard

title: AI-Powered Developer Portfolio
description: This portfolio, built with Next.js 14, 9 live-switching themes, and Sparky: an AI assistant powered by GPT-4o and a Pinecone RAG pipeline.
longDescription: An AI-powered portfolio built from scratch as a full-stack production application, not a template. The centerpiece is Sparky, an AI assistant backed by a GPT-4o + Pinecone RAG pipeline that answers natural language questions about projects, skills, and background via streaming SSE responses. The portfolio ships with 9 fully distinct visual themes (Cyberpunk AI, Terminal Hacker, Glassmorphism, Minimal Professional, and more) that switch live without a page reload. Visual details include matrix rain canvas effects, 3D tilt cards, typewriter animations, parallax scrolling, and staggered entrance animations. The contact form routes through Resend with a local JSON fallback. The project is open-source with a privacy-safe content architecture: all personal data lives in gitignored JSON files with placeholder commits, so anyone can clone it and make it their own.
highlights: 9 fully distinct visual themes with live switching: Cyberpunk, Terminal, Glassmorphism, Minimal, and more
AI assistant 'Sparky' powered by GPT-4o + Pinecone RAG with streaming responses
Matrix rain canvas, 3D tilt cards, typewriter effects, parallax scrolling, staggered animations
Open-source with privacy-safe content system: personal data gitignored, placeholder files committed
Contact form with Resend email delivery, local JSON fallback, and copy-to-sender option
